newsitem.title: UK: UK govt to make statement on London Underground.
newsitem.headline: UK govt to make statement on London Underground.

text.p: The British government will make a statement on the sell-off of London's underground rail network on Tuesday, Transport Secretary George Young said.
Young told BBC radio that the details of his statement would be announced in parliament later. "But I strongly believe the future of London Underground does rest in the private sector," he said.

He said privatisation would allow more money to be invested in the network and allow London Underground to plan for the long-term and not compete for public funds with health, education and other government priorities.
London Underground operates the capital's underground rail network, popularly known as the Tube.
Last week, London Underground chiefs complained of massive underinvestment from the government and listed hundreds of repair and improvement projects that have been shelved as a result.
They told politicians that funding for the next three years is about 700 million pounds less than they had expected. Young denied any reductions had been made in next year's budget.

Asked if the network would be sold if in one block or in a piecemeal fashion, Young said: "There are a number of options, all of which will drive up the amount of money available for investment, all of which will improve the service."

He noted that fares on privatised British Rail services had been kept under control through limits imposed on price rises. "If we go for the privatisation of London Underground, I would expect similar safeguards."
Through-ticketing, including travel cards that can be used on all lines, must also be safeguarded, he said.
"I think what we have in mind will be very popular with voters, very popular with passengers because it will improve the quality of public transport here in London," Young said.
The proposals are certainly being made with one eye on elections, due by May.
Earlier on Tuesday, the Times newspaper reported that the sale of London Underground would raise two billion pounds for reinvestment.
